papers.title: Effect of scan strategy on density and metallurgical properties of 17-4PH parts printed by Selective Laser Melting (SLM)
papers.first_author_affiliation: Faculty of Science, Engineering and Technology, Swinburne University of Technology, Victoria 3122, Australia

corresponding_authors.name: Rizwan Abdul Rahman Rashid
corresponding_authors.affiliation: Faculty of Science, Engineering and Technology, Swinburne University of Technology, Victoria 3122, Australia

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究SLM工艺参数对17-4PH钢密度和冶金性能的影响，未涉及生物医学植入物、多孔结构或应力遮挡。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not address porous structures for stress shielding, fatigue testing, surface roughness, osseointegration, or any biomedical context; it is purely about process parameters for a non-biomedical alloy.

summary_zh.motivation: 探究扫描策略对SLM成形17-4PH钢致密度的影响。
summary_zh.method: 采用不同扫描策略进行SLM实验，分析密度与微观组织。
summary_zh.result: 扫描策略显著影响孔隙率和相组成。
summary_zh.validation: 通过密度测量和金相观察验证结果。

summary_en.motivation: To investigate the influence of scan strategy on the density and metallurgical properties of 17-4PH stainless steel parts fabricated by selective laser melting.
summary_en.method: Different scan strategies (e.g., stripe, chessboard) were applied in SLM of 17-4PH, and the resulting density and microstructure were characterized.
summary_en.result: Scan strategy significantly affects porosity and phase composition, with optimal strategies achieving near-full density.
summary_en.validation: Validation was performed through density measurements (Archimedes method) and optical/electron microscopy of etched cross-sections.

papers.title: Cyclic plasticity and microstructure of as-built SLM Ti-6Al-4V: The effect of build orientation

corresponding_authors.name: Kyriakos I. Kourousis
corresponding_authors.affiliation: School of Engineering, RMIT University, Melbourne, Victoria, Australia

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究了选区激光熔化Ti-6Al-4V的循环塑性与显微组织，对生物医用植入体的疲劳性能评估具有参考价值，但未涉及多孔结构或应力遮挡。
llm.why_not_core: Does not link porous structure to stress shielding, lacks implant design or osseointegration context.

summary_zh.motivation: 研究成形方向对SLM Ti-6Al-4V循环塑性行为的影响
summary_zh.method: 对三种成形方向的试样进行应变控制循环试验及显微组织表征
summary_zh.result: 垂直方向试样循环软化更显著，位错结构差异导致各向异性
summary_zh.validation: 通过扫描电镜和透射电镜观察循环前后的微观结构变化

summary_en.motivation: Investigate the influence of build orientation on the cyclic plasticity and microstructural evolution of selective laser melted Ti-6Al-4V.
summary_en.method: Strain-controlled cyclic tests were conducted on specimens fabricated in three orientations, combined with microstructural characterization.
summary_en.result: Vertically built specimens exhibited more pronounced cyclic softening, attributed to orientation-dependent dislocation structures.
summary_en.validation: Microstructural observations via SEM and TEM before and after cycling confirmed the deformation mechanisms.

papers.title: Thermal stability and rheological properties of the ‘non-stick’ Caf1 biomaterial
papers.abstract: The ability to culture cells in three-dimensions has many applications, from drug discovery to wound healing. 3D cell culture methods often require appropriate scaffolds that mimic the cellular environments of different tissue types. The choice of material from which these scaffolds are made is of paramount importance, as its properties will define the manner in which cells interact with the scaffold. Caf1 is a protein polymer that is secreted from its host organism, Yersinia pestis, to enable escape from phagocytosis. In vitro, cells adhere poorly to the protein unless adhesion motifs are specifically introduced. Caf1 is a good candidate biomaterial due to its definable bioactivity, economical production and its ability to form hydrogels, through the use of cross-linkers. In this study, the thermostability of Caf1 was tested over a range of chemical conditions, and an initial characterisation of its rheological properties conducted in order to assess the suitability of Caf1 as a biomedical material. The results show that Caf1 retains its high thermostability even in harsh conditions such as extremes of pH, high salt concentrations and the presence of detergents. In solution, the concentrated polymer behaves as a complex viscous liquid. Due to these properties, Caf1 polymers are compatible with 3D bioprinting technologies and could be made to form a stimuli-responsive biomaterial that can alter its macrorheological properties in response to external factors. Caf1 biomaterials could therefore prove useful as 3D cell scaffolds for use in cell culture and wound repair.

summary_en.motivation: To assess the suitability of Caf1 protein polymer as a biomaterial for 3D cell culture scaffolds.

papers.title: [Three-dimensional bioprinted microstructure promotes proliferation and viability of murine epithelial stem cells in vitro].
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the effect of different microstructures prepared by three-dimensional (3D) bioprinting on proliferation and viability of the murine epithelial stem cells in vitro. METHODS: 3D cell-laden microstructures were constructed using 3 different printing nozzles with diameters of 210, 340, and 420 µm. Fluorescence microscopy and the live/dead assay kit were used to observe the proliferation and viability of the murine epithelial stem cells in the microstructures. RESULTS: All the 3D cell-laden micro-structures were capable of promoting the proliferation of murine epithelial stem cells. In the 3 groups of micro-structures, the cell viability decreased significantly with time until 7 days after printing (P<0.01), but at 14 days after the printing, the cell viability increased significantly as compared with that at 7 days (P<0.01). The viability of the cells was significantly higher in the microstructure printed using a 420 µm nozzle than in the microstructures printed with 210 µm and 340 µm nozzles (P<0.01). CONCLUSION: The microstructure printed with a 420 µm nozzle can stably promote the proliferation of murine epithelial stem cells and maintain a high level of cell viability, suggesting the feasibility of constructing tissue-engineered epidermis and full-thickness skin graft using 3D bioprinting technique.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文未涉及任何AI或机器学习方法，仅关注生物打印微观结构对细胞存活率的影响，与AI驱动生物打印方向无关。
llm.why_not_core: This paper contains no AI/ML integration into any bioprinting workflow stage; it is purely an experimental study on nozzle size effects on cell viability.

summary_zh.motivation: 探究3D生物打印不同喷嘴直径对小鼠上皮干细胞增殖和存活的影响。
summary_zh.method: 使用210、340、420 µm三种喷嘴打印含细胞微结构，荧光显微镜和活/死试剂盒评估。
summary_zh.result: 420 µm喷嘴打印的微结构能稳定促进细胞增殖并维持高存活率。
summary_zh.validation: 体外实验验证，统计比较不同时间点和喷嘴组的细胞存活率。

summary_en.motivation: To evaluate the effect of different nozzle diameters in 3D bioprinting on proliferation and viability of murine epithelial stem cells.
summary_en.method: Three cell-laden microstructures were printed using nozzles of 210, 340, and 420 µm, and cell viability was assessed via fluorescence microscopy and live/dead assay.
summary_en.result: The microstructure printed with a 420 µm nozzle significantly promoted cell proliferation and maintained higher viability compared to smaller nozzles.
summary_en.validation: In vitro live/dead staining and statistical analysis (P<0.01) at multiple time points up to 14 days post-printing.
